rule: Weekly review flags Foster training monotony (mean/SD of daily sRPE load) > 2 as a question or focus point.
summary: Foster 1998 linked illness mainly to individually identifiable strain thresholds (load x monotony), not to a fixed monotony cutoff. An IOC-subgroup systematic review lists increased training monotony as a risk factor for acute respiratory illness, and immune position statements recommend variety to limit monotony. The '> 2' number is a practitioner convention; the retrieved papers do not support it. The flag only starts a conversation, so it is cheap to keep. Pairing it with strain and the athlete's own history would be more faithful to Foster.

sources.note: Foster 1998 (n=25): illnesses mostly followed individual strain thresholds; defines monotony; no universal cutoff in the abstract.
Derman 2022 IOC-subgroup systematic review (48 studies): increased training monotony is associated with acute respiratory illness.
Walsh 2011 immune position statement: add variety to limit training monotony and strain.
Foster 2001: session-RPE is a valid load measure across exercise types (basis for the calculation).
